units.zh: 尉遲敬德 秦叔寶 程知節 段志玄 張公謹 子大素 大安
units.en: Yuchi Jingde, Qin Shubao, Cheng Zhijie, Duan Zhixuan, and Zhang Gongjin; Zhang's sons Dasu and Da'an.
units.literal: Yuchi Jingde, Qin Shubao, Cheng Zhijie, Duan Zhixuan, Zhang Gongjin; sons Dasu and Da'an.

units.zh: 尉遲敬德，朔州善陽人。
units.en: Yuchi Jingde came from Shanyang in Shuozhou.
units.literal: Yuchi Jingde was a native of Shanyang in Shuozhou.

units.zh: 大業末，從軍於高陽，討捕群賊，以武勇稱，累授朝散大夫。
units.en: Near the end of the Sui, he enlisted at Gaoyang to hunt down bandits, won renown for his fighting skill, and rose repeatedly to the rank of Chaosan dafu.
units.literal: At the end of the Daye reign he joined the army at Gaoyang, hunted down bandit groups, was famed for martial valor, and was repeatedly appointed Chaosan dafu.

units.zh: 劉武周起，以為偏將，與宋金剛南侵，陷晉、澮二州。
units.en: When Liu Wuzhou rebelled, Jingde served him as a deputy general; marching south with Song Jingang, they seized Jin and Hui prefectures.
units.literal: When Liu Wuzhou rose, Jingde was made a deputy general; with Song Jingang he invaded south and captured the two prefectures of Jin and Hui.

units.zh: 敬德深入，至夏縣，應接呂崇茂，襲破永安王孝基，執獨孤懷恩、唐儉等。
units.en: Jingde advanced deep into Tang territory as far as Xia County, joined forces with Lü Chongmao, routed Prince of Yong'an Xiaoji, and captured Dugu Huai'en, Tang Jian, and others.
units.literal: Jingde pressed deep, reaching Xia County, linking with Lü Chongmao, raiding and defeating Prince of Yong'an Xiaoji, and seizing Dugu Huai'en, Tang Jian, and others.

units.zh: 武德三年，太宗討武周於柏壁，武周令敬德與宋金剛來拒王師於介休。
units.en: In Wude year 3, when the Prince of Qin attacked Wuzhou at Baibi, Wuzhou sent Jingde and Song Jingang to block the imperial army at Jiexiu.
units.literal: In the third year of Wude, Taizong attacked Wuzhou at Baibi; Wuzhou ordered Jingde and Song Jingang to meet the imperial army at Jiexiu.

units.zh: 金剛戰敗，奔於突厥；
units.en: Song Jingang was beaten and fled to the Turks;
units.literal: Jingang was defeated in battle and fled to the Turks;

units.zh: 敬德收其餘眾，城守介休。
units.en: Jingde rallied the survivors and defended Jiexiu behind its walls.
units.literal: Jingde gathered the remaining troops and held Jiexiu behind city walls.

units.zh: 太宗遣任城王道宗、宇文士及往諭之。
units.en: The Prince of Qin sent Prince of Rencheng Li Daozong and Yuwen Shiji to negotiate his surrender.
units.literal: Taizong sent the Prince of Rencheng Li Daozong and Yuwen Shiji to instruct him.

units.zh: 敬德與尋相舉城來降。
units.en: Jingde and Xun Xiang surrendered the city to the Tang.
units.literal: Jingde and Xun Xiang surrendered the city and came over.

units.zh: 太宗大悅，賜以曲宴，引為右一府統軍，從擊王世充於東都。
units.en: The prince was delighted, gave him a private banquet, made him commander of the Right First Office, and took him east to fight Wang Shichong.
units.literal: Taizong was greatly pleased, granted him a private feast, appointed him commander of the Right First Office, and had him follow in the attack on Wang Shichong at the Eastern Capital.

units.zh: 既而尋相與武周下降將皆叛，諸將疑敬德必叛，囚於軍中。
units.en: Soon Xun Xiang and other former Liu Wuzhou officers rebelled; the Tang generals assumed Jingde would follow and threw him in chains.
units.literal: Soon afterward Xun Xiang and the surrendered generals of Wuzhou all rebelled; the commanders suspected Jingde would surely rebel too and imprisoned him in the army.

units.zh: 行台左僕射屈突通、尚書殷開山咸言：「敬德初歸國家，情志未附。
units.en: Qutu Tong, left vice director of the executive department, and Yin Kaishan, a minister, both urged: "Jingde has only just come over; his loyalty is still uncertain.
units.literal: Left Vice Director of the Executive Department Qutu Tong and Minister Yin Kaishan both said: "Jingde has only lately submitted to the state; his feelings are not yet attached.

units.zh: 此人勇健非常，縶之又久，既被猜貳，怨望必生。
units.en: He is ferociously strong; kept bound this long, he will surely turn resentful once he feels we distrust him.
units.literal: This man is extraordinarily brave and strong; he has been bound a long time, and once doubly suspected, resentment is sure to arise.

units.zh: 留之恐貽後悔，請即殺之。」
units.en: If we keep him we may regret it—execute him now."
units.literal: Keeping him may bring later regret; please kill him at once."

units.zh: 太宗曰：「寡人所見，有異於此。
units.en: The prince replied: "I see the matter differently.
units.literal: Taizong said: "What I see differs from this.

units.zh: 敬德若懷翻背之計，豈在尋相之後耶？」
units.en: If Jingde meant to betray us, would he have waited until after Xun Xiang rebelled?"
units.literal: If Jingde harbored a plan to turn traitor, would it come only after Xun Xiang?"

units.zh: 遽命釋之，引入臥內，賜以金寶，謂曰：「丈夫以意氣相期，勿以小疑介意。
units.en: He had Jingde freed at once, brought him into his private quarters, and gave him gold and gems, saying: "Men of honor trust one another's spirit; do not let petty doubts weigh on you.
units.literal: He immediately ordered him released, brought him into his sleeping quarters, bestowed gold and jewels, and said: "Men pledge themselves by spirit and resolve; do not let small suspicions trouble your mind.

units.zh: 寡人終不聽讒言以害忠良，公宜體之。
units.en: I will never listen to slander against a loyal man—you must believe that.
units.literal: I will never heed slander to harm the loyal and worthy; you should understand this.

units.zh: 必應欲去，今以此物相資，表一時共事之情也。」
units.en: If you truly mean to leave, take these gifts as proof of the bond we shared in service together."
units.literal: If you surely wish to leave, I now use these things to support you, showing the feeling of our time working together."

units.zh: 是日，因從獵於榆窠，遇王世充領步騎數萬來戰。
units.en: That same day, on a hunt at Yuke, Wang Shichong attacked with tens of thousands of foot and horse.
units.literal: That day, while hunting at Yuke, they met Wang Shichong leading tens of thousands of infantry and cavalry to battle.

units.zh: 世充驍將單雄信領騎直趨太宗，敬德躍馬大呼，橫刺雄信墜馬。
units.en: Wang's champion Shan Xiongxin charged straight at the prince; Jingde spurred forward with a shout and knocked Xiongxin from the saddle with a sideways thrust.
units.literal: Shichong's fierce general Shan Xiongxin led cavalry straight at Taizong; Jingde leapt his horse, shouted loudly, and thrust crosswise, knocking Xiongxin from his horse.

units.zh: 賊徒稍卻，敬德翼太宗以出賊圍。
units.en: The enemy fell back a little; Jingde shielded the prince and broke him out of the encirclement.
units.literal: The rebels drew back slightly; Jingde shielded Taizong and brought him out of the rebel encirclement.

units.zh: 更率騎兵與世充交戰，數合，其眾大潰，擒偽將陳智略，獲排槊兵六千人。
units.en: He led the cavalry back into the fight; after several clashes Wang's army broke completely; they captured the rebel general Chen Zhilüe and six thousand pike troops.
units.literal: He again led cavalry to fight Shichong; after several engagements the enemy force collapsed in great rout; the false general Chen Zhilüe was captured and six thousand pike-bearing soldiers were taken.

units.zh: 太宗謂敬德曰：「比眾人證公必叛，天誘我意，獨保明之，福善有征，何相報之速也！」
units.en: The prince told him: "Everyone swore you would turn traitor; Heaven moved me to trust you alone—good deeds bring their reward, and how fast you have repaid me!"
units.literal: Taizong said to Jingde: "Just now everyone testified you would surely rebel; Heaven guided my intent and I alone kept you clear—blessing the good has proof; how swiftly you repay!"

units.zh: 特賜金銀一篋，此後恩眄日隆。
units.en: He gave him a chest of gold and silver; from then on Jingde's favor grew day by day.
units.literal: He specially bestowed a chest of gold and silver; thereafter favor and regard grew daily.

units.zh: 敬德善解避槊，每單騎入賊陣，賊槊攢刺，終不能傷，又能奪取賊槊，還以刺之。
units.en: Jingde was a master of parrying the lance: riding alone into enemy ranks, he would emerge unhurt though spears thrust at him from every side, and he could seize a foe's lance and stab back with it.
units.literal: Jingde was skilled at evading the lance; each time he entered the rebel lines alone, rebel lances thrust together yet could not harm him; he could also seize rebel lances and turn them back to stab.

units.zh: 是日，出入重圍，往返無礙。
units.en: That day he passed through ring after ring of encirclement as if unimpeded.
units.literal: That day he went in and out of heavy encirclements, coming and going without hindrance.

units.zh: 齊王元吉亦善馬槊，聞而輕之，欲親自試，命去槊刃，以竿相刺。
units.en: Prince of Qi Li Yuanji, himself skilled with the cavalry lance, heard of this and scoffed; he wanted a personal trial and had the blades removed so they would spar with blunted poles.
units.literal: Prince of Qi Yuanji was also skilled with the mounted lance; hearing this he belittled him and wished to test in person, ordering the lance blades removed and using poles to thrust at each other.

units.zh: 敬德曰：「縱使加刃，終不能傷。
units.en: Jingde said: "Even with real blades you still could not touch me.
units.literal: Jingde said: "Even if blades were added, in the end you could not harm me.

units.zh: 請勿除之，敬德槊謹當卻刃。」
units.en: Leave the blades on—I will blunt mine instead."
units.literal: Please do not remove them; Jingde's lance will carefully turn the edge back."

units.zh: 元吉竟不能中。
units.en: Yuanji could not land a single hit.
units.literal: Yuanji in the end could not strike him.

units.zh: 太宗問曰：「奪槊、避槊，何者難易？」
units.en: The prince asked: "Which is harder—seizing a lance or parrying one?"
units.literal: Taizong asked: "Seizing the lance and evading the lance—which is harder or easier?"

units.zh: 對曰：「奪槊難。」
units.en: He answered: "Seizing it is harder."
units.literal: He replied: "Seizing the lance is hard."

units.zh: 乃命敬德奪元吉槊。
units.en: He ordered Jingde to disarm Yuanji in a bout.
units.literal: He then ordered Jingde to seize Yuanji's lance.

units.zh: 元吉執槊躍馬，志在刺之，敬德俄頃三奪其槊。
units.en: Yuanji charged with his lance set to kill; in moments Jingde stripped it from him three times running.
units.literal: Yuanji grasped his lance, leapt his horse, intent on stabbing him; in a moment Jingde thrice seized his lance.

units.zh: 元吉素驍勇，雖相嘆異，甚以為恥。
units.en: Yuanji, himself a famed fighter, was astonished but deeply humiliated.
units.literal: Yuanji was by nature fierce and brave; though he marveled at him, he felt deep shame.

units.zh: 及竇建德營於板渚，太宗將挑戰，先伏李勣、程知節、秦叔寶等兵。
units.en: When Dou Jiande camped at Banzhu, the prince prepared an ambush with Li Ji, Cheng Zhijie, Qin Shubao, and others before offering battle.
units.literal: When Dou Jiande encamped at Banzhu, Taizong was about to offer battle and first hid the troops of Li Ji, Cheng Zhijie, Qin Shubao, and others.

units.zh: 太宗持弓矢，敬德執槊，造建德壘下大呼致師。
units.en: The prince took his bow while Jingde took his lance; they rode to Dou's camp and shouted a challenge.
units.literal: Taizong held bow and arrows; Jingde grasped the lance; they went to Jiande's ramparts and shouted loudly to summon battle.

units.zh: 賊眾大驚擾，出兵數千騎，太宗逡巡漸卻，前後射殺數人，敬德所殺亦十數人，遂引賊以入伏內。
units.en: The rebels panicked and sent out thousands of horsemen; the prince feigned retreat, killing several with his bow while Jingde killed a dozen more, luring the enemy into the trap.
units.literal: The rebel host was greatly alarmed and disturbed; they sent out several thousand cavalry; Taizong hesitated and gradually withdrew, shooting and killing several men before and behind; those Jingde killed also numbered more than ten; thus they drew the rebels into the ambush.

units.zh: 於是與勣等奮擊，大破之。
units.en: Then Li Ji and the hidden force charged and smashed Dou's army.
units.literal: Thereupon with Ji and the others they struck fiercely and routed them utterly.

units.zh: 王世充兄子偽代王琬，使於建德軍中，乘隋煬帝所御驄馬，鎧甲甚鮮，迥出軍前以誇眾。
units.en: Wang Shichong's nephew Wang Wan, the rebel Prince of Dai, was with Dou's army; he rode Emperor Yang's famous piebald stallion in gleaming armor, prancing before the lines to impress the troops.
units.literal: Wang Shichong's nephew the false Prince of Dai Wang Wan, envoy in Jiande's army, rode the piebald horse Emperor Yang of Sui had used, his armor very bright, standing far out before the army to display pride to the masses.

units.zh: 太宗曰：「彼之所乘，真良馬也。」
units.en: The prince said: "That is a fine horse he rides."
units.literal: Taizong said: "What that one rides is truly a fine horse."

units.zh: 敬德請往取之，乃與高甑生、梁建方三騎直入賊軍，擒琬，引其馬以歸，賊眾無敢當者。
units.en: Jingde volunteered to take it; with Gao Zengsheng and Liang Jianfang he charged straight into the enemy ranks, seized Wang Wan and his horse, and rode back unopposed.
units.literal: Jingde asked to go and seize it; then with Gao Zengsheng and Liang Jianfang the three riders plunged straight into the rebel army, captured Wan, led his horse back, and none of the rebel host dared oppose them.

units.zh: 又從討劉黑闥於臨洺，黑闥軍來襲李世勣，太宗勒兵掩賊，復以救之。
units.en: He fought again at Linming against Liu Heita; when Heita's force attacked Li Shiji, the prince moved to strike the rebels and sent Jingde to the rescue.
units.literal: He again followed in the campaign against Liu Heita at Linming; Heita's army came to attack Li Shiji; Taizong drove troops to cover the rebels and again went to rescue him.

units.zh: 既而黑闥眾至，其軍四合，敬德率壯士犯圍而入，大破賊陣，太宗與江夏王道宗乘之以出。
units.en: When Heita's army closed in from every side, Jingde led picked men through the ring, shattered the rebel formation, and brought the prince and Prince of Jiangxia Li Daozong out with him.
units.literal: Soon Heita's masses arrived and his army closed on all four sides; Jingde led stalwarts to break through the encirclement and enter, smashing the rebel formation; Taizong and the Prince of Jiangxia Li Daozong rode out on them.

units.zh: 又從破徐圓朗。
units.en: He also helped defeat Xu Yuanlang.
units.literal: He again followed in the defeat of Xu Yuanlang.

units.zh: 累有戰功，授秦王府左二副護軍。
units.en: After many victories he was made left second deputy protector-general of the Prince of Qin's household.
units.literal: With repeated battle achievements he was appointed Left Second Deputy Protector-General of the Prince of Qin's mansion.

units.zh: 隱太子、巢剌王元吉將謀害太宗，密緻書以招敬德曰：「願迂長者之眷，敦布衣之交，幸副所望也。」
units.en: The Hidden Crown Prince and the Nest-stinging Prince Yuanji plotted to harm Taizong and secretly wrote to win Jingde over: "We wish to divert the elder's regard and cultivate a commoner's friendship; may we have what we hope."
units.literal: The Hidden Crown Prince and the Nest-stinging Prince Yuanji were about to plot harm against Taizong; they secretly sent a letter to win Jingde, saying: "We wish to divert the elder's regard and cultivate a commoner's friendship; may it fulfill what is hoped."

units.zh: 仍贈以金銀器物一車。
units.en: They sent a cartload of gold, silver, and fine goods with the letter.
units.literal: They also presented a cartload of gold, silver, and vessels.

units.zh: 敬德辭曰：「敬德起自幽賤，逢遇隋亡，天下土崩，竄身無所，久淪逆地，罪不容誅。
units.en: Jingde refused: "I come from humble obscurity; when the Sui fell and the realm collapsed I had nowhere to turn and long served rebels—a crime for which even execution could not atone.
units.literal: Jingde declined, saying: "Jingde rose from obscure low birth; I met the fall of Sui, the realm's earth crumbling, with nowhere to hide myself; long sunk in rebel territory, my crime could not bear execution.

units.zh: 實荷秦王惠以生命，今又隸名籓邸，唯當以身報恩。
units.en: The Prince of Qin spared my life and took me into his household; I owe him my life and nothing else.
units.literal: I truly owe the Prince of Qin grace in sparing my life; now again listed in the prince's mansion, I can only repay with my body.

units.zh: 於殿下無功，不敢謬當重賜。
units.en: I have done nothing for Your Highness and dare not accept such rich gifts.
units.literal: Toward Your Highness I have no merit and dare not wrongly accept heavy gifts.

units.zh: 若私許殿下，便是二心，徇利忘忠，殿下亦何所用？」
units.en: If I secretly agreed to you I would be disloyal, trading duty for gain—what use would such a man be to you?"
units.literal: If I privately assented to Your Highness, that would be divided loyalty, pursuing profit and forgetting faithfulness—of what use would Your Highness make me?"

units.zh: 建成怒，是後遂絕。
units.en: Jiancheng was furious and cut off contact with him.
units.literal: Jiancheng was angry; thereafter they broke off.

units.zh: 敬德尋以啟聞，太宗曰：「公之素心，郁如山嶽，積金至斗，知公情不可移。
units.en: Jingde reported the offer at once; the prince said: "Your loyalty stands firm as a mountain; even a bushel of gold could not sway you—I know your heart.
units.literal: Jingde soon reported this to Taizong, who said: "Your constant heart is dense as mountains and hills; even gold piled to a bushel—I know your feeling cannot be moved.

units.zh: 送來但取，寧須慮也。
units.en: Take whatever they send; you need not hesitate.
units.literal: What they send, simply take; why need you worry?

units.zh: 若不然，恐公身不安。
units.en: If you refuse, they may move against you personally.
units.literal: If not, I fear your person will not be secure.

units.zh: 且知彼陰計，足為良策。」
units.en: And learning their secret plot is strategy in itself."
units.literal: Moreover, knowing their secret plot is strategy enough."

units.zh: 元吉等深忌敬德，令壯士往刺之。
units.en: Yuanji and his faction hated Jingde and sent assassins after him.
units.literal: Yuanji and the others deeply resented Jingde and ordered stalwarts to go stab him.

units.zh: 敬德知其計，乃重門洞開，安臥不動，賊頻至其庭，終不敢入。
units.en: Knowing their intent, he left his gates wide open and slept undisturbed; the killers came to his courtyard again and again but never dared enter.
units.literal: Jingde knew their plan; he then left his heavy gates wide open and lay at ease without moving; assassins repeatedly came to his courtyard yet in the end dared not enter.

units.zh: 元吉乃譖敬德於高祖，下詔獄訊驗，將殺之，太宗固諫得釋。
units.en: Yuanji denounced him to Emperor Gaozu, who had Jingde jailed for interrogation and was going to kill him; Taizong's firm remonstrance secured his release.
units.literal: Yuanji then slandered Jingde to Gaozu; an edict put him in prison for interrogation and he was to be killed; Taizong firmly remonstrated and secured his release.

units.zh: 會突厥侵擾烏城，建成舉元吉為將，密謀請太宗同送於昆明池，將加屠害。
units.en: When Turks raided Wucheng, Jiancheng named Yuanji commander and secretly planned to invite the prince to see them off at Kunming Pool and murder him there.
units.literal: When the Turks harassed Wucheng, Jiancheng nominated Yuanji as general; they secretly plotted to ask Taizong to see them off together at Kunming Pool and there add slaughter and harm.

units.zh: 敬德聞其謀，與長孫無忌遽啟太宗曰：「大王若不速正之，則恐被其所害，社稷危矣。」
units.en: Jingde learned of the plot and with Zhangsun Wuji urged the prince: "If you do not act at once, they will kill you and the realm will be lost."
units.literal: Jingde heard their plot; with Zhangsun Wuji he urgently reported to Taizong: "If the King does not quickly set things right, I fear you will be harmed by them and the altars of state will be in peril."

units.zh: 太宗嘆曰：「今二宮離阻骨肉，滅棄君親，危亡之機，共所知委。
units.en: The prince sighed: "My brothers have turned against kin and king; the danger is plain to everyone.
units.literal: Taizong sighed: "Now the two palaces estrange flesh and bone, destroy and abandon ruler and kin; the moment of peril and ruin is what all know and entrust.

units.zh: 寡人雖深被猜忌，禍在須臾，然同氣之情，終所未忍。
units.en: I am deeply suspected and death is near, yet I still cannot bring myself to harm my own brothers.
units.literal: Though I am deeply suspected and disaster hangs in an instant, yet the feeling of shared breath I have never yet been able to bear away.

units.zh: 欲待其先起，然後以義討之，公意以為何如？」
units.en: I mean to wait until they strike first, then move against them with justice—what do you think?"
units.literal: I wish to wait until they rise first, then with righteousness punish them—what does your view think?"

units.zh: 敬德曰：「人情畏死，眾人以死奉王，此天授也。
units.en: Jingde said: "Men fear death, yet these men are ready to die for you—that is Heaven's gift.
units.literal: Jingde said: "Human nature fears death; the masses offer death to serve the King—this is Heaven's grant.

units.zh: 若天與不取，反受其咎。
units.en: If Heaven offers and you refuse, you will answer for it.
units.literal: If Heaven grants and you do not take, you will instead receive its blame.

units.zh: 雖存仁愛之小情，忘社稷之大計，禍至而不恐，將亡而自安，失人臣臨難不避之節，乏先賢大義滅親之事，非所聞也。
units.en: To cherish private affection while forgetting the realm, to face ruin without fear, to neglect a subject's duty to meet peril head-on, to lack the sages' willingness to sacrifice kin for the state—such things I have never heard praised.
units.literal: Though you keep small feeling of benevolence and love, you forget the great plan of the altars of state; when disaster comes you are not afraid, about to perish yet self-assured—you lose a minister's integrity of not avoiding hardship, lack the former sages' great righteousness in extinguishing kin—this is not what I have heard.

units.zh: 以臣愚誠，請先誅之。
units.en: In all sincerity, I beg you to strike first.
units.literal: With this subject's foolish sincerity, I ask to execute them first.

units.zh: 王若不從，敬德言請奔逃亡命，不能交手受戮。
units.en: If you refuse, I must flee for my life—I will not stay to be butchered.
units.literal: If the King does not follow, Jingde says he asks to flee and save his life; he cannot meet blades and receive slaughter.

units.zh: 且因敗成功，明賢之高見；
units.en: To turn defeat into victory is the mark of a sage;
units.literal: Moreover, turning defeat into success is the lofty view of the bright and worthy;

units.zh: 轉禍為福，智士之先機。
units.en: to turn disaster into blessing is the wise man's foresight.
units.literal: turning calamity into blessing is the wise man's foresight.

units.zh: 敬德今若逃亡，無忌亦欲同去。」
units.en: If I run, Wuji means to run with me."
units.literal: If Jingde now flees, Wuji also wishes to go together."

units.zh: 太宗猶豫未決，無忌曰：「王今不從敬德之言，必知敬德等非王所有。
units.en: The prince still wavered; Wuji said: "If you reject Jingde now, you will lose him and all of us with him.
units.literal: Taizong hesitated and could not decide; Wuji said: "If the King now does not follow Jingde's words, you must know that Jingde and the others are not the King's to keep.

units.zh: 事今敗矣，其若之何？」
units.en: The cause is lost—what then?"
units.literal: The affair is now ruined—what is to be done?"

units.zh: 太宗曰：「寡人所言，未可全棄，公更圖之。」
units.en: The prince said: "Do not abandon my plan entirely—find another way."
units.literal: Taizong said: "What I have said cannot be wholly abandoned; you should plot further."

units.zh: 敬德曰：「王今處事有疑，非智；
units.en: Jingde said: "Hesitation in crisis is not wisdom;
units.literal: Jingde said: "The King now handles affairs with doubt—that is not wisdom;

units.zh: 臨難不決，非勇。
units.en: indecision before danger is not courage.
units.literal: facing hardship without decision—that is not courage.

units.zh: 王縱不從敬德言，請自決計，其如家國何？
units.en: Even if you reject my counsel, decide for yourself—what of the realm and your house?
units.literal: Even if the King does not follow Jingde's words, please decide for yourself—what of family and state?

units.zh: 其如身命何？
units.en: What of your own life?
units.literal: What of your person and life?

units.zh: 且在外勇士八百餘人，今悉入宮，控弦被甲，事勢已就，王何得辭！」
units.en: More than eight hundred armed men are already in the palace with bows drawn and armor on—the deed is ready; you cannot refuse!"
units.literal: Moreover, more than eight hundred stalwarts outside—now all have entered the palace, drawn bowstrings and donned armor; the situation is already set—how can the King decline!"

units.zh: 敬德又與侯君集日夜進勸，然後計定。
units.en: Jingde and Hou Junji pressed him day and night until the plan was fixed.
units.literal: Jingde again with Hou Junji day and night urged forward; only then was the plan settled.

units.zh: 時房玄齡、杜如晦皆被高祖斥出秦府，不得復入。
units.en: Fang Xuanling and Du Ruhui had been banished from the prince's household by the emperor and could not return.
units.literal: At that time Fang Xuanling and Du Ruhui had both been expelled by Gaozu from the Prince of Qin's mansion and could not re-enter.

units.zh: 太宗令長孫無忌密召之，玄齡等報曰：「有敕不許更事王，今若私謁，必至誅滅，不敢奉命。」
units.en: The prince sent Zhangsun Wuji to fetch them secretly; they replied: "We are forbidden to serve you again; a private visit would mean death—we dare not come."
units.literal: Taizong ordered Zhangsun Wuji to summon them secretly; Xuanling and the others replied: "There is an edict forbidding us to serve the King again; if we now visit privately, we will surely reach execution and extinction—we dare not obey the command."

units.zh: 太宗大怒，謂敬德曰：「玄齡、如晦豈背我耶？」
units.en: The prince flew into a rage and told Jingde: "Would Fang and Du betray me?"
units.literal: Taizong was greatly angry and said to Jingde: "Would Xuanling and Ruhui betray me?"

units.zh: 取所佩刀授敬德曰：「公且往，觀其無來心，可並斬其首持來也。」
units.en: He handed Jingde his own sword: "Go. If they will not come, cut off their heads and bring them here."
units.literal: He took the sword at his belt and gave it to Jingde, saying: "Sir, go for now; if you see they have no mind to come, you may together cut off their heads and bring them."

units.zh: 敬德又與無忌喻曰：「王已決計剋日平賊，公宜即入籌之。
units.en: Jingde told them through Wuji: "The prince has set the day to strike; come at once to plan with us.
units.literal: Jingde again with Wuji instructed them: "The King has already decided the day to pacify the rebels; you gentlemen should enter at once to plan it.

units.zh: 我等四人不宜群行在道。」
units.en: The four of us must not travel together on the road."
units.literal: We four should not travel the road in a group."

units.zh: 於是玄齡、如晦著道士服隨無忌入，敬德別道亦至。
units.en: Fang and Du entered in Taoist dress with Wuji; Jingde came by another route.
units.literal: Thereupon Xuanling and Ruhui wore Taoist robes and followed Wuji in; Jingde by another route also arrived.

units.zh: 六月四日，建成既死，敬德領七十騎躡踵繼至，元吉走馬東奔，左右射之墜馬。
units.en: On the fourth day of the sixth month, after Jiancheng was killed, Jingde pursued with seventy horsemen; Yuanji fled east and was shot from the saddle by the prince's men.
units.literal: On the fourth day of the sixth month, after Jiancheng was already dead, Jingde led seventy riders treading on his heels in pursuit; Yuanji spurred his horse fleeing east; those left and right shot him and he fell from his horse.

units.zh: 太宗所乘馬又逸於林下，橫被所繣，墜不能興。
units.en: The prince's horse bolted into the woods, caught on a vine, and threw him; he could not get up.
units.literal: Taizong's mount again bolted into the woods below; it was caught crosswise by what tethered it, and he fell, unable to rise.

units.zh: 元吉遽來奪弓，垂欲相扼，敬德躍馬叱之，於是步走，欲歸武德殿，敬德奔逐射殺之。
units.en: Yuanji rushed to seize the bow and nearly throttled the prince; Jingde spurred up shouting; Yuanji fled on foot toward Wude Hall and Jingde overtook and shot him dead.
units.literal: Yuanji hurried to seize the bow; about to throttle each other, Jingde leapt his horse and shouted at him; Yuanji then walked on foot, wishing to return to Wude Hall; Jingde ran in pursuit and shot and killed him.

units.zh: 其宮府諸將薛萬徹、謝叔方、馮立等率兵大至，屯於玄武門，殺屯營將軍。
units.en: The generals of Jiancheng's and Yuanji's palace establishments, Xue Wanche, Xie Shufang, Feng Li, and others, marched up in force to Xuanwu Gate and killed the garrison commander.
units.literal: The generals of their palaces Xue Wanche, Xie Shufang, Feng Li, and others led troops in great numbers arriving, encamped at Xuanwu Gate, and killed the garrison camp general.

units.zh: 敬德持建成、元吉首以示之，宮府兵遂散。
units.en: Jingde displayed Jiancheng's and Yuanji's heads; the palace-establishment troops thereupon scattered.
units.literal: Jingde held the heads of Jiancheng and Yuanji to show them; the palace troops thereupon dispersed.

units.zh: 是時，高祖泛舟於海池。
units.en: Meanwhile Emperor Gaozu was boating on the imperial pond.
units.literal: At that time Gaozu was boating on the Sea Pool.

units.zh: 太宗命敬德侍衛高祖。
units.en: The prince sent Jingde to guard the emperor.
units.literal: Taizong ordered Jingde to attend and guard Gaozu.

units.zh: 敬德擐甲持矛，直至高祖所。
units.en: Jingde strode to the emperor in full armor with spear in hand.
units.literal: Jingde donned armor and grasped spear, going straight to where Gaozu was.

units.zh: 高祖大驚，問曰：「今日作亂是誰？
units.en: The emperor was startled and demanded: "Who has risen in revolt today?
units.literal: Gaozu was greatly startled and asked: "Who is making trouble today?

units.zh: 卿來此何也？」
units.en: Why have you come here like this?"
units.literal: Why have you come here?"

units.zh: 對曰：「秦王以太子、齊王作亂，舉兵誅之，恐陛下驚動，遣臣來宿衛。」
units.en: He answered: "The Prince of Qin has put down a revolt by the crown prince and Prince of Qi. Fearing Your Majesty might be alarmed, he sent me to guard you."
units.literal: He replied: "The Prince of Qin, because the Crown Prince and Prince of Qi made rebellion, raised troops to execute them; fearing Your Majesty would be alarmed, he sent me to guard overnight."

units.zh: 高祖意乃安。
units.en: The emperor's fears subsided.
units.literal: Gaozu's mind then grew calm.

units.zh: 南衙、北門兵馬及二宮左右猶相拒戰，敬德奏請降手敕，令諸軍兵並受秦王處分，於是內外遂定。
units.en: Fighting still raged between palace guards and Eastern Palace forces; Jingde obtained an imperial order placing all troops under the prince's command, and the realm was pacified.
units.literal: The troops of the Southern Yamen, Northern Gate, and the two palaces' attendants still opposed each other in battle; Jingde memorialized asking for a handwritten edict to be issued, ordering all armies to accept the Prince of Qin's disposition; thus inside and outside were settled.

units.zh: 高祖勞敬德曰：「卿於國有安社稷之功。」
units.en: The emperor praised him: "You have saved the dynasty."
units.literal: Gaozu comforted Jingde, saying: "You have the achievement of securing the altars of state for the realm."

units.zh: 賜珍物甚眾。
units.en: He showered him with rich gifts.
units.literal: He bestowed many precious things.

units.zh: 太宗升春宮，授太子左衛率。
units.en: When the prince became heir apparent, he made Jingde commander of the crown prince's left guard.
units.literal: When Taizong ascended the Eastern Palace, he appointed him Left Guard Commander of the Crown Prince.

units.zh: 時議者以建成等左右百餘人，併合從坐籍沒，唯敬德執之不聽，曰：「為罪者二凶，今已誅訖，若更及支黨，非取安之策。」
units.en: Many urged that Jiancheng's hundred-odd followers be punished and their property seized; Jingde alone objected: "Only the two culprits deserved death; to punish their whole circle is no way to secure peace."
units.literal: At the time debaters held that Jiancheng's attendants, more than a hundred, should together be implicated and their property confiscated; only Jingde held to it and would not listen, saying: "Those guilty are the two villains, now already executed; if we extend further to branches and factions, that is not a policy to secure peace."

units.zh: 由是獲免。
units.en: Thanks to him they were spared.
units.literal: Through this they obtained exemption.

units.zh: 及論功，敬德與長孫無忌為第一，各賜絹萬匹；
units.en: In the distribution of rewards Jingde and Zhangsun Wuji ranked first, each receiving ten thousand bolts of silk;
units.literal: When merits were discussed, Jingde and Zhangsun Wuji ranked first, each granted ten thousand bolts of silk;

units.zh: 齊王府財幣器物，封其全邸，盡賜敬德。
units.en: and the entire treasury of Prince of Qi Li Yuanji's mansion was sealed and given to Jingde.
units.literal: the wealth, currency, and vessels of the Prince of Qi's mansion were sealed in its whole residence and entirely bestowed on Jingde.

units.zh: 貞觀元年，拜右武候大將軍，賜爵吳國公，與長孫無忌、房玄齡、杜如晦四人並食實封千三百戶。
units.en: In Zhenguan 1 he became right martial guard grand general and Duke of Wu; he and Zhangsun Wuji, Fang Xuanling, and Du Ruhui each held substantive fiefs of 1,300 households.
units.literal: In the first year of Zhenguan he was appointed Right Martial Guard Grand General, enfeoffed as Duke of Wu, and with Zhangsun Wuji, Fang Xuanling, and Du Ruhui the four together received substantive fiefs of thirteen hundred households.

units.zh: 會突厥來入寇，授涇州道行軍總管以擊之。
units.en: When Turks invaded, he was made commander on campaign of the Jingzhou circuit.
units.literal: When the Turks came to invade, he was appointed Commander on Campaign of the Jingzhou Circuit to strike them.

units.zh: 賊至涇陽，敬德輕騎與之挑戰，殺其名將，賊遂敗。
units.en: At Jingyang he met them with light cavalry, killed their champion, and routed them.
units.literal: The rebels reached Jingyang; Jingde with light cavalry challenged them in battle, killed their famed general, and the rebels were defeated.

units.zh: 敬德好訐直，負其功，每見無忌、玄齡、如晦等短長，必面折廷辯，由是與執政不平。
units.en: Jingde was blunt and proud of his merit; he openly quarreled with Zhangsun Wuji, Fang Xuanling, and Du Ruhui in court and fell out with the chief ministers.
units.literal: Jingde loved blunt straightness and relied on his achievements; whenever he saw Wuji, Xuanling, Ruhui, and others' faults and merits, he would invariably face them down in court debate; thus he was at odds with those in power.

units.zh: 三年，出為襄州都督。
units.en: In year 3 he was posted as military governor of Xiangzhou.
units.literal: In the third year he went out as Military Governor of Xiangzhou.

units.zh: 八年，累遷同州刺史。
units.en: By year 8 he had risen to governor of Tongzhou.
units.literal: In the eighth year he was repeatedly promoted to Governor of Tongzhou.

units.zh: 嘗侍宴慶善宮，時有班在其上者，敬德怒曰：「汝有何功，合坐我上？」
units.en: At a feast in Qingshan Palace he flew into a rage when someone whose place in the seating order was above him sat there: "What have you done that you should sit above me?"
units.literal: Once while attending a feast at Qingshan Palace, when there was someone whose place in the rank-order was above him, Jingde angrily said: "What achievement have you, that you should sit above me?"

units.zh: 任城王道宗次其下，因解喻之。
units.en: Prince of Rencheng Li Daozong, seated below, tried to calm him.
units.literal: Prince of Rencheng Li Daozong was ranked below him and therefore explained and admonished him.

units.zh: 敬德勃然，拳毆道宗目，幾至眇。
units.en: Jingde struck Daozong in the eye and nearly blinded him.
units.literal: Jingde erupted and with his fist struck Daozong in the eye, nearly blinding him.

units.zh: 太宗不懌而罷，謂敬德曰：「朕覽漢史，見高祖功臣獲全者少，意常尤之。
units.en: The emperor ended the feast in displeasure and told Jingde: "Reading Han history, I have long regretted how few of Gaozu's meritorious followers died in peace.
units.literal: Taizong was displeased and ended the feast; he said to Jingde: "I have read Han history and see that few of Gaozu's meritorious ministers were preserved whole—I have often blamed this.

units.zh: 及居大位以來，常欲保全功臣，令子孫無絕。
units.en: Since taking the throne I have wanted to keep my meritorious men alive and their lines unbroken.
units.literal: Since occupying the great position I have often wished to preserve meritorious ministers and let their descendants not be cut off.

units.zh: 然卿居官輒犯憲法，方知韓、彭夷戮，非漢祖之愆。
units.en: Yet you break the law again and again—I see now that Han Xin and Peng Yue were not killed without cause.
units.literal: Yet you in office repeatedly violate the statutes; only then do I know Han Xin and Peng Yue's extermination was not Han Gaozu's fault.

units.zh: 國家大事，唯賞與罰，非分之恩，不可數行，勉自修飭，無貽後悔也。」
units.en: The state rests on reward and punishment alone; favor beyond merit cannot be granted often—mend your ways before you regret it."
units.literal: The great affairs of state rely only on reward and punishment; undue favor cannot be repeatedly granted—strive to discipline yourself and bring no later regret."

units.zh: 十一年，封建功臣為代襲刺史，冊拜敬德宣州刺史，改封鄂國公。
units.en: In year 11 he was enfeoffed as hereditary prefect of Xuanzhou and made Duke of E.
units.literal: In the eleventh year meritorious ministers were enfeoffed as hereditary prefects; Jingde was appointed by patent as Prefect of Xuanzhou and his fief changed to Duke of E.

units.zh: 後歷鄜、夏二州都督。
units.en: He later governed Fu and Xia prefectures.
units.literal: Later he served in succession as Military Governor of Fu and Xia prefectures.

units.zh: 十七年，抗表乞骸骨，授開府儀同三司，令朝朔望。
units.en: In year 17 he petitioned to retire and was made Grand Master Equal to the Three Palaces (kaifu yitong sansi), attending court on the first and fifteenth.
units.literal: In the seventeenth year he submitted a memorial resisting and begging to retire; he was granted Grand Master with Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon of the First Order, and ordered to attend court on the first and fifteenth of the month.

units.zh: 尋與長孫無忌等二十四人圖形於凌煙閣。
units.en: He was among the twenty-four men portrayed at Lingyan Pavilion.
units.literal: Soon he and Zhangsun Wuji and twenty-two others had their portraits painted at Lingyan Pavilion.

units.zh: 及太宗將征高麗，敬德奏言：「車駕若自往遼左，皇太子又在定州，東西二京，府庫所在，雖有鎮守，終是空虛。
units.en: When the emperor planned to invade Goryeo, Jingde warned: "If Your Majesty goes to Liaodong while the crown prince is at Dingzhou, the two capitals where the treasuries lie will be left dangerously thin despite garrisons.
units.literal: When Taizong was about to campaign against Goryeo, Jingde memorialized: "If the imperial carriage goes in person to Liaodong, and the crown prince is again at Dingzhou, the eastern and western capitals where the treasuries lie—though there are garrisons, in the end they are empty.

units.zh: 遼東路遙，恐有玄感之變。
units.en: The long march east invites a rebellion like Yang Xuangan's.
units.literal: The road to Liaodong is far; I fear there may be an uprising like Xuangan's.

units.zh: 且邊隅小國，不足親勞萬乘，伏請委之良將，自可應時摧滅。」
units.en: This petty border kingdom is not worth the Son of Heaven's personal labor—send able generals and they will crush it in due course."
units.literal: Moreover a small state on the border fringe is not worth the ten-thousand-chariot ruler laboring in person; I humbly ask to entrust it to good generals, who of themselves can destroy it in season."

units.zh: 太宗不納，令以本官行太常卿，為左一馬軍總管，從破高麗於駐蹕山。
units.en: The emperor refused and made him acting grand master of ceremonies and left first cavalry commander on the campaign that defeated Goryeo at Mount Zhubi.
units.literal: Taizong did not accept it; he ordered him to act as Grand Master of Ceremonies in his regular office, as Left First Cavalry Commander, following to defeat Goryeo at Zhubeishan.

units.zh: 軍還，依舊致仕。
units.en: After the campaign he retired again.
units.literal: When the army returned, he resumed retirement as before.

units.zh: 敬德末年篤信仙方，飛煉金石，服食雲母粉，穿築池台，崇飾羅綺，嘗奏清商樂以自奉養，不與外人交通，凡十六年。
units.en: In his last years he pursued alchemy, took mica powder, built lavish gardens, lived in luxury, played court music for his own pleasure, and shunned visitors for sixteen years.
units.literal: In Jingde's later years he devoutly believed immortal formulas, smelted metal and stone, ingested powdered mica, built pools and terraces, adorned himself with brocades, once presented pure Shang music to nourish himself, and did not interact with outsiders—for sixteen years in all.

units.zh: 顯慶三年，高宗以敬德功，追贈其父為幽州都督。
units.en: In Xianqing 3 Emperor Gaozong enfeoffed his father posthumously as military governor of Youzhou.
units.literal: In the third year of Xianqing, Emperor Gaozong because of Jingde's merit posthumously enfeoffed his father as Military Governor of Youzhou.

units.zh: 其年薨，年七十四。
units.en: He died that year at seventy-four.
units.literal: That year he died, aged seventy-four.

units.zh: 高宗為之舉哀，廢朝三日，令京官五品以上及朝集使赴宅哭，冊贈司徒、并州都督，謚曰忠武，賜東園秘器，陪葬於昭陵。
units.en: Gaozong mourned him, closed court three days, ordered officials of the fifth rank and above and tribute envoys to attend his funeral, and posthumously made him Minister of Education (Situ) and military governor of Bingzhou with the posthumous name Loyal and Martial; he was buried at Zhaoling with imperial funeral honors.
units.literal: Emperor Gaozong held mourning for him, suspended court for three days, ordered capital officials of the fifth rank and above and tribute envoys to go to his residence to weep; by patent he was posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Works and Military Governor of Bingzhou, posthumous name Zhongwu, bestowed eastern-garden secret vessels, and buried with honor at Zhaoling.

units.zh: 子寶琳嗣，官至衛尉卿。
units.en: His son Baolin succeeded him and rose to commandant of the guards.
units.literal: His son Baolin inherited, reaching the office of Commandant of the Guards.

units.zh: 秦叔寶，名瓊，齊州歷城人。
units.en: Qin Shubao, whose name was Qiong, came from Licheng in Qizhou.
units.literal: Qin Shubao, personal name Qiong, was a native of Licheng in Qizhou.

units.zh: 大業中，為隋將來護兒帳內。
units.en: During the Daye reign he served in the guard of the Sui general Lai Hu'er.
units.literal: In the Daye reign he served in the tent retinue of the Sui general Lai Hu'er.

units.zh: 叔寶喪母，護兒遣使吊之，軍吏怪曰：「士卒死亡及遭喪者多矣，將軍未嘗降問，獨吊叔寶何也？」
units.en: When Shubao's mother died, Lai Hu'er sent condolences; his officers wondered: "Many soldiers have died or lost kin—why has the general never sent condolences except to Shubao?"
units.literal: When Shubao's mother died, Hu'er sent an envoy to condole; the army officers wondered: "Among soldiers many die or suffer bereavement—why has the general never lowered inquiry except to condole Shubao?"

units.zh: 答曰：「此人勇悍，加有志節，必當自取富貴，豈得以卑賤處之？」
units.en: He answered: "This man is brave and has true spirit; he will rise to wealth and honor—do not treat him as a common soldier."
units.literal: He replied: "This man is brave and fierce, and moreover has will and integrity; he will surely win wealth and honor for himself—how can one treat him as base and lowly?

units.zh: 隋末群盜起，從通守張須陀擊賊帥盧明月於下邳。
units.en: When rebellion spread at the end of the Sui, he followed Zhang Xuantuo against the rebel Lu Mingyue at Xiapi.
units.literal: At the end of Sui bandits rose everywhere; he followed Defender-in-chief Zhang Xuantuo to strike the bandit chief Lu Mingyue at Xiapi.

units.zh: 賊眾十餘萬，須陀所統才萬人，力勢不敵，去賊六七里立柵，相持十餘日，糧盡將退，謂諸將士曰：「賊見兵卻，必輕來追我。
units.en: The rebels numbered over 100,000 against Xuantuo's 10,000; after ten days' stalemate with food running out, he told his men: "When they see us withdraw they will pursue lightly.
units.literal: The rebel host was more than a hundred thousand; what Xuantuo commanded was only ten thousand men; strength and momentum could not match; they left the rebels six or seven li and set up palisades, facing off more than ten days; provisions exhausted, about to withdraw; he said to the officers and soldiers: "When the rebels see the army retreat, they will surely come lightly to pursue us.

units.zh: 其眾既出，營內即虛，若以千人襲營，可有大利。
units.en: Their camp will be empty—if a thousand men strike it, we can win greatly.
units.literal: Once their masses have come out, the camp within is empty; if a thousand men raid the camp, there can be great profit.

units.zh: 此誠危險，誰能去者？」
units.en: It is dangerous—who will go?"
units.literal: This is truly dangerous—who can go?"

units.zh: 人皆莫對，唯叔寶與羅士信請行。
units.en: No one spoke until Shubao and Luo Shixin volunteered.
units.literal: No one answered; only Shubao and Luo Shixin asked to go.

units.zh: 於是須陀委柵遁，使二人分領千兵伏於蘆葦間。
units.en: Xuantuo withdrew, leaving them each with 1,000 men hidden in the reeds.
units.literal: Thereupon Xuantuo abandoned the palisade and fled, sending the two to command a thousand men each in ambush among the reeds.

units.zh: 既而明月果悉兵追之，叔寶與士信馳至其柵，柵門閉不得入，二人超升其樓，拔賊旗幟，各殺數人，營中大亂。
units.en: Mingyue pursued with his whole army; the two galloped to his camp, scaled the gate tower when the gates closed, tore down his banners, killed several men, and threw the camp into chaos.
units.literal: Soon Mingyue as expected led all his troops in pursuit; Shubao and Shixin galloped to his palisade; the gate was closed and they could not enter; the two leapt onto its tower, pulled down rebel banners, each killed several men, and the camp fell into great disorder.

units.zh: 叔寶、士信又斬關以納外兵，因縱火焚其三十餘柵，煙焰漲天。
units.en: They broke the gate for the main force and burned more than thirty stockades until the sky was black with smoke.
units.literal: Shubao and Shixin again cut through the gate to admit outside troops, and set fire burning more than thirty palisades; smoke and flame filled the sky.

units.zh: 明月奔還，須陀又回軍奮擊，大破賊眾。
units.en: Mingyue fled back; Xuantuo counterattacked and routed the rebels.
units.literal: Mingyue ran back; Xuantuo turned the army and struck fiercely, routing the rebel host utterly.

units.zh: 明月以數百騎遁去，余皆虜之。
units.en: Mingyue escaped with a few hundred horsemen; the rest were captured.
units.literal: Mingyue escaped with several hundred cavalry; the rest were all captured.

units.zh: 由是勇氣聞於遠近。
units.en: His fame for courage spread far and wide.
units.literal: Thus his courage was heard far and near.

units.zh: 又擊孫宣雅於海曲，先登破之。
units.en: He again led the assault that broke Sun Xuanya at Haiqu.
units.literal: He again struck Sun Xuanya at Haiqu, taking the lead in the assault and breaking them.

units.zh: 以前後累勳授建節尉。
units.en: For repeated merit he was made a Jianjie commandant.
units.literal: For accumulated merits before and after he was appointed Jianjie wei.

units.zh: 從須陀進擊李密於滎陽，軍敗，須陀死之，叔寶以餘眾附裴仁基。
units.en: He followed Xuantuo against Li Mi at Xingyang; when Xuantuo was killed, Shubao joined Pei Renji.
units.literal: Following Xuantuo he advanced to strike Li Mi at Xingyang; the army was defeated and Xuantuo died; Shubao with the remaining troops attached to Pei Renji.

units.zh: 會仁基以武牢降於李密，密得叔寶大喜，以為帳內驃騎，待之甚厚。
units.en: When Renji surrendered Wulao to Li Mi, Mi was delighted and made Shubao a flying-cavalry general in his guard, treating him generously.
units.literal: When Renji surrendered Wulao to Li Mi, Mi gained Shubao and was greatly pleased, making him tent-retinue Flying Cavalry general and treating him very generously.

units.zh: 密與化及大戰於黎陽童山，為流矢所中，墮馬悶絕。
units.en: In a great battle with Yu Huaji at Tongshan in Liyang, Mi was struck by a stray arrow and fell unconscious from his horse.
units.literal: Mi fought a great battle with Yu Huaji at Tongshan in Liyang and was struck by a stray arrow; he fell from his horse and lost consciousness.

units.zh: 左右奔散，追兵且至，唯叔寶獨捍衛之，密遂獲免。
units.en: His guards fled; pursuers were closing in; only Shubao defended him until Mi was safe.
units.literal: Those left and right scattered in flight; pursuing troops were about to arrive; only Shubao alone defended him, and Mi thus escaped harm.

units.zh: 叔寶又收兵與之力戰，化及乃退。
units.en: Shubao rallied troops and fought Yu Huaji off.
units.literal: Shubao again gathered troops and fought with him with force; Huaji then withdrew.

units.zh: 後密敗，又為王世充所得，署龍驤大將軍。
units.en: After Mi's defeat Wang Shichong took him and made him dragon-soaring grand general.
units.literal: Later when Mi was defeated, he again came into Wang Shichong's possession and was appointed Dragon-soaring Grand General.

units.zh: 叔寶薄世充之多詐，因其出抗官軍，至於九曲，與程咬金、吳黑闥、牛進達等數十騎西馳百許步，下馬拜世充曰：「雖蒙殊禮，不能仰事，請從此辭。」
units.en: Shubao despised Shichong's deceit; at Jiuqu, with Cheng Yaojin, Wu Heita, Niu Jinda, and dozens of riders, he rode west, dismounted, and said: "Though you have honored me, I cannot serve you—I take my leave."
units.literal: Shubao despised Shichong's much deceit; when Shichong went out to resist the imperial army, reaching Jiugqu, with Cheng Yaojin, Wu Heita, Niu Jinda, and several tens of riders he galloped west more than a hundred paces, dismounted and bowed to Shichong: "Though I have received extraordinary favor, I cannot serve you with head raised—please let me take leave from here."

units.zh: 世充不敢逼，於是來降。
units.en: Shichong did not dare stop them, and they defected to the Tang.
units.literal: Shichong did not dare press them; thus they came to surrender.

units.zh: 高祖令事秦府，太宗素聞其勇，厚加禮遇。
units.en: Gaozu assigned him to the Prince of Qin; the prince, knowing his fame, honored him richly.
units.literal: Gaozu ordered him to serve the Prince of Qin's mansion; Taizong had long heard of his courage and treated him with thick courtesy.

units.zh: 從鎮長春宮，拜馬軍總管。
units.en: He garrisoned Changchun Palace as cavalry commander.
units.literal: He followed in garrisoning Changchun Palace and was appointed Cavalry Commander.

units.zh: 又從征於美良川，破尉遲敬德，功最居多。
units.en: At Meiliang River he defeated Yuchi Jingde and won the greatest credit.
units.literal: He again followed on campaign at Meiliang River, defeating Yuchi Jingde, his achievements ranking the most.

units.zh: 高祖遣使賜以金瓶，勞之曰：「卿不顧妻子，遠來投我，又立功效。
units.en: Gaozu sent a golden bottle and said: "You left your family to join me from afar and have served brilliantly.
units.literal: Gaozu sent an envoy bestowing a golden bottle and comforted him: "You disregarded wife and children, came from afar to join me, and again established achievements.

units.zh: 朕肉可為卿用者，當割以賜卿，況子女玉帛乎？
units.en: If my own flesh could help you I would cut it off for you—how much more mere wealth?
units.literal: Flesh of my body that can be used for you—I would cut and bestow it; how much more sons and daughters, jade, and silk?

units.zh: 卿當勉之。」
units.en: Press on."
units.literal: You should strive hard."

units.zh: 尋授秦王右三統軍。
units.en: He was soon made the prince's right third commander.
units.literal: Soon he was appointed the Prince of Qin's Right Third Commander.

units.zh: 又從破宋金剛於介休。
units.en: He helped defeat Song Jingang at Jiexiu.
units.literal: He again followed in defeating Song Jingang at Jiexiu.

units.zh: 錄前後勳，賜黃金百斤、雜彩六千段，授上柱國。
units.en: For his cumulative merit he received a hundred jin of gold, six thousand lengths of silk, and the title supreme pillar of state.
units.literal: Recording merits before and after, he was granted a hundred jin of gold and six thousand lengths of mixed silks, and appointed Supreme Pillar of State.

units.zh: 從討王世充，每為前鋒。
units.en: In the war on Wang Shichong he always led the van.
units.literal: Following the campaign against Wang Shichong, he was always in the vanguard.

units.zh: 太宗將拒竇建德於武牢，叔寶以精騎數十先陷其陣。
units.en: At Hulao he led several dozen elite horsemen in the first charge that broke Dou Jiande's line.
units.literal: When Taizong was about to resist Dou Jiande at Hulao, Shubao with several tens of elite cavalry first broke their formation.

units.zh: 世充平，進封翼國公，賜黃金百斤、帛七千段。
units.en: After Shichong's fall he was made Duke of Yi with a hundred jin of gold and seven thousand lengths of silk.
units.literal: When Shichong was pacified, he was advanced to Duke of Yi, granted a hundred jin of gold and seven thousand lengths of silk.

units.zh: 從平劉黑闥，賞物千段。
units.en: For Liu Heita's defeat he received a thousand lengths of goods.
units.literal: Following the pacification of Liu Heita, he was rewarded with a thousand lengths of goods.

units.zh: 叔寶每從太宗征伐，敵中有驍將銳卒，炫耀人馬，出入來去者，太宗頗怒之，輒命叔寶往取。
units.en: On campaign, whenever enemy champions paraded before the lines, the prince would send Shubao to bring them down.
units.literal: Whenever Shubao followed Taizong on campaign, if among the enemy there were fierce generals and sharp soldiers who displayed men and horses, coming and going, Taizong was often angered and would order Shubao to go take them.

units.zh: 叔寶應命，躍馬負槍而進，必刺之萬眾之中，人馬辟易，太宗以是益重之，叔寶亦以此頗自矜尚。
units.en: Shubao would charge in, invariably killing them in the midst of the host; the prince prized him all the more, and Shubao grew somewhat proud of it.
units.literal: Shubao answered the command, leapt his horse bearing lance and advanced, invariably stabbing them amid ten thousand men; men and horses gave way; Taizong therefore valued him more; Shubao also for this was somewhat self-admiring.

units.zh: 六月四日，從誅建成、元吉。
units.en: On the fourth day of the sixth month he took part in killing Jiancheng and Yuanji.
units.literal: On the fourth day of the sixth month he followed in executing Jiancheng and Yuanji.

units.zh: 事寧，拜左武衛大將軍，食實封七百戶。
units.en: After the coup he became left martial guard grand general with a substantive fief of seven hundred households.
units.literal: When affairs were settled he was appointed Left Martial Guard Grand General with a substantive fief of seven hundred households.

units.zh: 其後每多疾病，因謂人曰：「吾少長戎馬，所經二百餘陣，屢中重瘡。
units.en: Later he was often ill and said: "I have fought in more than two hundred battles since youth and been gravely wounded many times.
units.literal: Afterward he often had many illnesses; he therefore said to people: "I from youth grew up in war horses; the campaigns I passed through numbered more than two hundred; repeatedly I received grave wounds.

units.zh: 計吾前後出血亦數斛矣，安得不病乎？」
units.en: I have lost several hu of blood in all—no wonder I am sick."
units.literal: Counting the blood I have shed before and after, it also amounts to several hu—how could I not be ill?"

units.zh: 十二年卒，贈徐州都督，陪葬昭陵。
units.en: He died in year 12 and was buried at Zhaoling with posthumous rank as military governor of Xuzhou.
units.literal: In the twelfth year he died; he was posthumously granted the office of Military Governor of Xuzhou and buried with honor at Zhaoling.

units.zh: 太宗特令所司就其塋內立石人馬，以旌戰陣之功焉。
units.en: Taizong ordered stone men and horses erected at his tomb to commemorate his battlefield deeds.
units.literal: Taizong specially ordered the relevant office to erect stone men and horses at his tomb mound to proclaim achievements in battle arrays.

units.zh: 十三年，改封胡國公。
units.en: In year 13 his title was changed to Duke of Hu.
units.literal: In the thirteenth year his fief was changed to Duke of Hu.

units.zh: 十七年，與長孫無忌等圖形於凌煙閣。
units.en: In year 17 his portrait was painted at Lingyan Pavilion.
units.literal: In the seventeenth year he and Zhangsun Wuji and others had their portraits at Lingyan Pavilion.

units.zh: 程知節，本名咬金，濟州東阿人也。
units.en: Cheng Zhijie, originally named Yaojin, came from Dong'e in Jizhou.
units.literal: Cheng Zhijie, original personal name Yaojin, was a native of Dong'e in Jizhou.

units.zh: 少驍勇，善用馬槊。
units.en: As a youth he was fierce and skilled with the cavalry lance.
units.literal: In youth he was fierce and brave, skilled in using the mounted lance.

units.zh: 大業末，聚徒數百，共保鄉里，以備他盜。
units.en: Near the end of the Sui he gathered several hundred men to defend his home district.
units.literal: At the end of Daye he gathered several hundred followers, together protecting the village against other bandits.

units.zh: 後依李密，署為內軍驃騎。
units.en: He later joined Li Mi and became a flying-cavalry officer of the inner army.
units.literal: Later he attached to Li Mi and was appointed as Inner Army Flying Cavalry.

units.zh: 時密於軍中簡勇士尤異者八千人，隸四驃騎，分為左右以自衛，號為內軍。
units.en: Mi chose eight thousand of his bravest men for four flying-cavalry units, left and right, as his personal guard—the inner army.
units.literal: At the time Mi in the army selected eight thousand warriors of exceptional valor as the four Flying Cavalry, divided into left and right to guard himself, called the Inner Army.

units.zh: 自云：「此八千人可當百萬。」
units.en: He boasted: "These eight thousand can match a million."
units.literal: He himself said: "These eight thousand men can match a million."

units.zh: 知節既領其一，甚被恩遇。
units.en: Zhijie commanded one unit and was highly favored.
units.literal: Zhijie then commanded one of them and was greatly favored.

units.zh: 及王世充出城決戰，知節領內馬軍，與密同營在北邙山上，單雄信領外馬軍，營在偃師城北。
units.en: When Wang Shichong offered battle outside the city, Zhijie led the inner cavalry and camped with Mi on Mount Beimang while Shan Xiongxin camped north of Yanshi with the outer cavalry.
units.literal: When Wang Shichong came out of the city for a decisive battle, Zhijie commanded the inner horse army; with Mi he encamped together on Mount Beimang; Shan Xiongxin commanded the outer horse army, encamped north of Yanshi city.

units.zh: 世充來襲雄信營，密遣知節及裴行儼助之。
units.en: Shichong attacked Xiongxin's camp; Mi sent Zhijie and Pei Xingyan to help.
units.literal: Shichong came to raid Xiongxin's camp; Mi sent Zhijie and Pei Xingyan to assist.

units.zh: 行儼先馳赴敵，為流矢所中，墜於地。
units.en: Xingyan charged first, was hit by a stray arrow, and fell.
units.literal: Xingyan first galloped to meet the enemy and was struck by a stray arrow, falling to the ground.

units.zh: 知節救之，殺數人，世充軍披靡，乃抱行儼重騎而還。
units.en: Zhijie rescued him, killed several men, scattered Wang's troops, lifted Xingyan back onto his horse, and withdrew.
units.literal: Zhijie rescued him, killed several men; Shichong's army scattered; he then embraced Xingyan, remounted, and returned.

units.zh: 為世充騎所逐，刺槊洞過，知節回身捩折其槊，兼斬獲追者，於是與行儼俱免。
units.en: Shichong's horsemen pursued; a lance pierced through him; Zhijie turned, broke the lance, killed his pursuers, and both escaped.
units.literal: Pursued by Shichong's cavalry, a thrusting lance pierced through; Zhijie turned and wrenched the lance broken, also cutting down those who pursued; thus he and Xingyan both escaped.

units.zh: 及密敗，世充得之，接遇甚厚。
units.en: After Mi's defeat Wang Shichong took him in and treated him well.
units.literal: When Mi was defeated, Shichong obtained him and received him very generously.

units.zh: 知節謂秦叔寶曰：「世充器度淺狹，而多妄語，好為咒誓，乃巫師老嫗耳，豈是撥亂主乎？」
units.en: Zhijie told Qin Shubao: "Shichong is narrow-minded, full of empty talk and oaths like an old witch—how could he be a ruler who ends chaos?"
units.literal: Zhijie said to Qin Shubao: "Shichong's breadth of mind is shallow and narrow, and he has much false speech; he loves to make curses and oaths—he is but an old witch; how could he be a lord who settles turmoil?"

units.zh: 及世充拒王師於九曲，知節領兵在其陣，與秦叔寶等馬上揖世充曰：「荷公接待，極欲報恩。
units.en: When Shichong resisted the imperial army at Jiuqu, Zhijie commanded troops in his formation; with Qin Shubao and others he bowed to Shichong from horseback and said: "You have treated us well and we wished to repay you—
units.literal: When Shichong resisted the imperial army at Jiugqu, Zhijie commanded troops in his formation; with Qin Shubao and others on horseback they bowed to Shichong: "We owe Your Grace reception and greatly wish to repay favor.

units.zh: 公性猜貳，傍多扇惑，非僕託身之所，今謹奉辭。」
units.en: but you are suspicious and easily swayed; this is no place for us—we take our leave."
units.literal: Your nature is suspicious and divided, with many beside you stirring confusion—this is not where I entrust my person; I now respectfully take leave."

units.zh: 於是躍馬與左右數十人歸國，世充懼，不敢追之。
units.en: They galloped off with several dozen men to the Tang; Shichong feared to pursue.
units.literal: Thereupon they spurred their horses and with several tens on left and right returned to the state; Shichong was afraid and did not dare pursue.

units.zh: 授秦王府左三統軍。
units.en: He became left third commander of the Prince of Qin's household.
units.literal: He was appointed Left Third Commander of the Prince of Qin's mansion.

units.zh: 破宋金剛，擒竇建德，降王世充，並領左一馬軍總管。
units.en: He defeated Song Jingang, captured Dou Jiande, and helped reduce Wang Shichong, serving as left first cavalry commander.
units.literal: Defeating Song Jingang, capturing Dou Jiande, and reducing Wang Shichong, he also held the post of Left First Cavalry Commander.

units.zh: 每陣先登，以功封宿國公。
units.en: He led every charge and was enfeoffed as Duke of Su.
units.literal: In every battle he took the lead in the assault; for achievements he was enfeoffed as Duke of Su.

units.zh: 武德七年，建成忌之，構之於高祖，除康州刺史。
units.en: In Wude 7 Jiancheng slandered him to Gaozu and he was banished to Kangzhou.
units.literal: In the seventh year of Wude, Jiancheng resented him; he framed him before Gaozu, and he was removed to Prefect of Kangzhou.

units.zh: 知節白太宗曰：「大王手臂今並翦除，身必不久。
units.en: Zhijie told Taizong: "Your Highness's supporting arms have now all been cut away; you yourself cannot last long.
units.literal: Zhijie told Taizong plainly: "The King's arms are now all cut away; your person cannot last long.

units.zh: 知節以死不去，願速自全。」
units.en: He vowed to die rather than leave and urged the prince to save himself at once."
units.literal: Zhijie would not leave even at death and urged swift self-preservation."

units.zh: 六月四日，從太宗討建成、元吉。
units.en: On the fourth day of the sixth month he joined the prince in killing Jiancheng and Yuanji.
units.literal: On the fourth day of the sixth month he followed Taizong in punishing Jiancheng and Yuanji.

units.zh: 事定，拜太子右衛率，遷右武衛大將軍，賜實封七百戶。
units.en: After the coup he became crown prince right guard commander, then right martial guard grand general, with a fief of seven hundred households.
units.literal: When affairs were settled he was appointed Right Guard Commander of the Crown Prince, promoted to Right Martial Guard Grand General, granted a substantive fief of seven hundred households.

units.zh: 貞觀中，歷瀘州都督、左領軍大將軍。
units.en: Under Zhenguan he governed Luzhou and became left leading army grand general.
units.literal: In the Zhenguan reign he served in succession as Military Governor of Luzhou and Left Leading Army Grand General.

units.zh: 與長孫無忌等代襲刺史，改封盧國公，授普州刺史。
units.en: He was among the hereditary prefects and was made Duke of Lu and prefect of Pu.
units.literal: With Zhangsun Wuji and others he received hereditary prefectships; his fief was changed to Duke of Lu and he was appointed Prefect of Pu.

units.zh: 十七年，累轉左屯衛大將軍，檢校北門屯兵，加鎮軍大將軍。
units.en: In year 17 he became left tunwei grand general, inspector of the northern gate garrison, and grand general who pacifies the army.
units.literal: In the seventeenth year he was repeatedly transferred to Left Tunwei Grand General, inspected the northern gate garrison troops, and added Grand General Who Pacifies the Army.

units.zh: 永徽六年，遷左衛大將軍。
units.en: In Yonghui 6 he became left guard grand general.
units.literal: In the sixth year of Yonghui he was transferred to Left Guard Grand General.

units.zh: 顯慶二年，授蔥山道行軍大總管以討賀魯。
units.en: In Xianqing 2 he commanded the Congshan circuit campaign against Helu.
units.literal: In the second year of Xianqing he was appointed Commander on Campaign of the Congshan Circuit to punish Helu.

units.zh: 師次怛篤城，有胡人數千家開門出降，知節屠城而去，賀魯遂即遠遁。
units.en: At Dudu City thousands of Hu surrendered; Zhijie massacred the city and Helu fled.
units.literal: The army halted at Dudu City; several thousand households of Hu opened the gates and surrendered; Zhijie slaughtered the city and left; Helu thereupon fled far away.

units.zh: 軍還，坐免官。
units.en: On return he was dismissed for the massacre.
units.literal: When the army returned, he was removed from office for the offense.

units.zh: 未幾，授岐州刺史。
units.en: He was soon made prefect of Qi.
units.literal: Before long he was appointed Prefect of Qi.

units.zh: 表請乞骸骨，許之。
units.en: He petitioned to retire and was allowed.
units.literal: He memorialized begging to retire; this was granted.

units.zh: 麟德二年卒，贈驃騎大將軍、益州大都督，陪葬昭陵。
units.en: He died in Linde 2 and was buried at Zhaoling with posthumous rank as flying-cavalry grand general and grand protector-general of Yizhou.
units.literal: In the second year of Linde he died; posthumously enfeoffed as Flying Cavalry Grand General and Grand Protector-General of Yizhou, buried with honor at Zhaoling.

units.zh: 子處默，襲爵盧國公。
units.en: His son Chumo inherited the dukedom of Lu.
units.literal: His son Chumo inherited the Duke of Lu.

units.zh: 處亮，以功臣子尚太宗女清河長公主，授駙馬都尉、左衛中郎將。
units.en: Chuliang, as the son of a meritorious minister, married Emperor Taizong's daughter the Grand Princess of Qinghe, and was appointed Commandant of the Horse and Left Guard Commandant of the Palace Gentlemen.
units.literal: Chuliang, as son of a meritorious minister, married Emperor Taizong's daughter the Grand Princess of Qinghe, was appointed Commandant of the Horse and Left Guard Commandant of the Palace Gentlemen.

units.zh: 少子處弼，官至右金吾將軍。
units.en: The youngest son Chubi rose to right golden raven general.
units.literal: The youngest son Chubi reached the office of Right Golden Raven General.

units.zh: 處弼子伯獻，開元中，左金吾大將軍。
units.en: Chubi's son Boxian was left golden raven grand general under Kaiyuan.
units.literal: Chubi's son Boxian, in the Kaiyuan reign, was Left Golden Raven Grand General.

units.zh: 段志玄，齊州臨淄人也。
units.en: Duan Zhixuan came from Linzi in Qizhou.
units.literal: Duan Zhixuan was a native of Linzi in Qizhou.

units.zh: 父偃師，隋末為太原郡司法書佐，從高祖起義，官至郢州刺史。
units.en: His father Yanshi, a Taiyuan judicial clerk in late Sui, followed Gaozu in the uprising and became prefect of Yingzhou.
units.literal: His father Yanshi in late Sui was judicial clerk of Taiyuan commandery; he followed Gaozu in raising righteousness and reached the office of Prefect of Yingzhou.

units.zh: 志玄從父在太原，甚為太宗所接待。
units.en: Zhixuan followed his father at Taiyuan and was greatly received by Taizong.
units.literal: Zhixuan followed his father at Taiyuan and was greatly received by Taizong.

units.zh: 義兵起，志玄募得千餘人，授右領大都督府軍頭。
units.en: At the uprising he raised over a thousand men and became an army head in the right leading office.
units.literal: When the righteous army rose, Zhixuan recruited more than a thousand men and was appointed Army Head of the Right Leading Grand Protector-General's Office.

units.zh: 從平霍邑，下絳郡，攻永豐倉，皆為先鋒，歷遷左光祿大夫。
units.en: He was vanguard at Huoyi, Jiang, and Yongfeng granary and rose to left glory grand master.
units.literal: Following in the pacification of Huoyi, taking Jiang commandery, and attacking the Yongfeng granary, he was always vanguard and was repeatedly promoted to Left Glory Grand Master.

units.zh: 從劉文靜拒屈突通於潼關，文靜為通將桑顯和所襲，軍營已潰，志玄率二十騎赴擊，殺數十人而還。
units.en: At Tong Pass, when Liu Wenjing's camp collapsed under Sang Xianhe, Zhixuan charged with twenty riders, killed dozens, and withdrew.
units.literal: Following Liu Wenjing in resisting Qu Tuotong at Tong Pass, when Wenjing was struck by Tong's general Sang Xianhe, the army camp was already routed; Zhixuan led twenty riders to strike, killed several tens, and returned.

units.zh: 為流矢中足，慮眾心動，忍而不言，更入賊陣者再三。
units.en: Shot in the foot, he hid the wound and charged the enemy lines repeatedly.
units.literal: Struck by a stray arrow in the foot, fearing the masses' hearts would stir, he endured without speaking and entered the rebel formation again and again.

units.zh: 顯和軍亂，大軍因此復振，擊，大破之。
units.en: The enemy line broke; the Tang army rallied and routed them.
units.literal: Xianhe's army fell into disorder; the great army thereby revived and struck, routing them utterly.

units.zh: 及屈突通之遁，志玄與諸將追而擒之，以功授樂游府驃騎將軍。
units.en: When Qutu Tong fled, Zhixuan with the generals pursued and captured him; for merit he was appointed Flying Cavalry General of the Leyou garrison.
units.literal: When Qu Tuotong fled, Zhixuan with the generals pursued and captured him; for merit he was appointed Flying Cavalry General of Leyou Prefecture.

units.zh: 後從討王世充，深入陷陣，馬倒，為賊所擒。
units.en: Campaigning against Wang Shichong, he was thrown and captured when his horse fell.
units.literal: Later following the campaign against Wang Shichong, he pressed deep into the formation; his horse fell and he was captured by rebels.

units.zh: 兩騎夾持其髻，將渡洛水，志玄踴身而奮，二人俱墜馬，馳歸，追者數百騎，不敢逼。
units.en: Two rebels seized his hair to drag him across the Luo; he fought free, both fell, he escaped, and hundreds of pursuers dared not close.
units.literal: Two riders held his topknot and were about to cross the Luo River; Zhixuan leapt and struggled; both fell from their horses; he galloped back; several hundred pursuing riders did not dare press.

units.zh: 及破竇建德，平東都，功又居多。
units.en: When Dou Jiande was defeated and the Eastern Capital pacified, his achievements again ranked among the greatest.
units.literal: When Dou Jiande was defeated and the Eastern Capital pacified, his achievements again ranked the most.

units.zh: 遷秦王府右二護軍，賞物二千段。
units.en: He became right second protector-general of the Qin mansion with two thousand lengths of goods.
units.literal: He was transferred to Right Second Protector-General of the Prince of Qin's mansion, rewarded with two thousand lengths of goods.

units.zh: 隱太子建成、巢剌王元吉競以金帛誘之，志玄拒而不納，密以白太宗，竟與尉遲敬德等同誅建成、元吉。
units.en: Jiancheng and Yuanji tried to buy him with gold; he refused and warned the prince, then joined Jingde in killing them.
units.literal: The Hidden Crown Prince Jiancheng and Nest-stinging Prince Yuanji both competed to entice him with gold and silk; Zhixuan refused and did not accept, secretly reporting to Taizong; in the end with Yuchi Jingde and others alike he executed Jiancheng and Yuanji.

units.zh: 太宗即位，累遷左驍衛大將軍，封樊國公，食實封九百戶。
units.en: When Taizong ascended the throne he was repeatedly promoted to Left Xiaoqi Grand General, enfeoffed as Duke of Fan, with a substantive fief of nine hundred households.
units.literal: When Taizong ascended the throne he was repeatedly promoted to Left Xiaoqi Grand General, enfeoffed as Duke of Fan, with a substantive fief of nine hundred households.

units.zh: 文德皇后之葬也，志玄與宇文士及分統士馬出肅章門。
units.en: At Empress Wende's funeral he and Yuwen Shiji commanded troops leaving Suxiang Gate.
units.literal: At the burial of Empress Wende, Zhixuan with Yuwen Shiji divided command of troops and horses out through Suxiang Gate.

units.zh: 太宗夜使宮官至二將軍所，士及開營內使者，志玄閉門不納，曰：「軍門不可夜開。」
units.en: The emperor sent a night messenger; Shiji admitted him but Zhixuan barred the gate: "The camp gate does not open at night."
units.literal: Taizong at night sent a palace official to the two generals' posts; Shiji opened the camp to the inner envoy; Zhixuan closed the gate and would not admit him, saying: "The army gate cannot be opened at night."

units.zh: 使者曰：「此有手敕。」
units.en: The envoy said: "Here is a handwritten edict."
units.literal: The envoy said: "Here is a handwritten edict."

units.zh: 志玄曰：「夜中不辯真偽。」
units.en: Zhixuan replied: "At night one cannot tell real from false."
units.literal: Zhixuan said: "In the night one cannot distinguish true from false."

units.zh: 竟停使者至曉。
units.en: He held the envoy until dawn.
units.literal: He finally detained the envoy until dawn.

units.zh: 太宗聞而嘆曰：「此真將軍也，周亞夫無以加焉。」
units.en: The emperor praised him: "A true general—Zhou Yafu was no better."
units.literal: Taizong heard and sighed: "This is a true general; Zhou Yafu cannot surpass him."

units.zh: 十一年，定世封之制，授金州刺史，改封褒國公。
units.en: In year 11 he was made hereditary prefect of Jinzhou and Duke of Bao.
units.literal: In the eleventh year the system of hereditary enfeoffments for the age was fixed; he was appointed Prefect of Jinzhou and his fief changed to Duke of Bao.

units.zh: 十二年，拜右衛大將軍。
units.en: In year 12 he became right guard grand general.
units.literal: In the twelfth year he was appointed Right Guard Grand General.

units.zh: 十四年，加鎮軍大將軍。
units.en: In year 14 he was made grand general who pacifies the army.
units.literal: In the fourteenth year he was added Grand General Who Pacifies the Army.

units.zh: 十六年，寢疾，太宗親自臨視，涕泣而別，顧謂曰：「當與卿子五品。」
units.en: In year 16, gravely ill, he was visited by the weeping emperor, who as he left said: "I shall give your son fifth rank."
units.literal: In the sixteenth year he lay ill; Taizong personally came to visit, wept in parting, and turning said: "I shall give your son fifth rank."

units.zh: 志玄頓首固請回授母弟志感，太宗遂授志感左衛郎將。
units.en: Zhixuan kowtowed and firmly asked to transfer it to his mother's younger brother Zhigan; Taizong thereupon appointed Zhigan Left Guard Gentleman.
units.literal: Zhixuan kowtowed and firmly asked to transfer it to his mother's younger brother Zhigan; Taizong thereupon appointed Zhigan Left Guard Gentleman.

units.zh: 及卒，上為發哀，哭之甚慟，贈輔國將軍、揚州都督，陪葬昭陵，謚曰忠壯。
units.en: At his death the emperor mourned deeply, enfeoffed him posthumously as general who assists the state and military governor of Yangzhou with the name Loyal and Strong, and buried him at Zhaoling.
units.literal: When he died the emperor held mourning, wept very bitterly, posthumously enfeoffed him as General Who Assists the State and Military Governor of Yangzhou, buried with honor at Zhaoling, posthumous name Zhongzhuang.

units.zh: 十七年正月，詔圖形於凌煙閣。
units.en: In the first month of year 17 his portrait joined Lingyan Pavilion.
units.literal: In the first month of the seventeenth year an edict ordered his portrait at Lingyan Pavilion.

units.zh: 子瓚，襲爵褒國公，武太后時，官至左屯衛大將軍。
units.en: His son Zan inherited the dukedom and rose to left tunwei grand general under Empress Wu.
units.literal: His son Zan inherited the Duke of Bao; in Empress Wu's time he reached Left Tunwei Grand General.

units.zh: 子懷簡，襲爵，開元中，官至太子詹事。
units.en: His son Huaijian inherited and became crown prince household minister under Kaiyuan.
units.literal: His son Huaijian inherited the fief; in the Kaiyuan reign he reached Crown Prince Household Minister.

units.zh: 張公謹，字弘慎，魏州繁水人也。
units.en: Zhang Gongjin, courtesy name Hongshen, came from Fanshui in Weizhou.
units.literal: Zhang Gongjin, style Hongshen, was a native of Fanshui in Weizhou.

units.zh: 初為王世充洧州長史。
units.en: He first served Wang Shichong as chief administrator of Wei prefecture.
units.literal: Initially he was Chief Administrator of Wei prefecture under Wang Shichong.

units.zh: 武德元年，與王世充所署洧州刺史崔樞以州城歸國，授鄒州別駕，累除右武候長史。
units.en: In Wude 1 he and Cui Shu surrendered Wei to the Tang; he became vice prefect of Zou and rose to chief of the right martial guard.
units.literal: In the first year of Wude, with Cui Shu, whom Shichong had appointed Prefect of Wei, he surrendered the prefectural city to the state; he was appointed Vice Prefect of Zou, repeatedly promoted to Chief of the Right Martial Guard.

units.zh: 初未知名，李勣尉遲敬德亦言之，乃引入幕府。
units.en: At first he was not yet known by name; Li Ji and Yuchi Jingde also spoke of him, and he was then brought into the staff headquarters.
units.literal: At first he was not yet known by name; Li Jiji and Yuchi Jingde also spoke of him, and he was then brought into the staff headquarters.

units.zh: 時太宗為隱太子建成、巢王元吉所忌，因召公謹，問以自安之策，對甚合旨，漸見親遇。
units.en: When Jiancheng and Yuanji threatened him, he asked Gongjin for counsel; the answers pleased him and he grew intimate with him.
units.literal: At the time Taizong was resented by the Hidden Crown Prince Jiancheng and Prince of Qi Yuanji; he therefore summoned Gongjin and asked strategies for self-preservation; the replies very much matched his intent and he was gradually seen with intimate favor.

units.zh: 及太宗將討建成、元吉，遣卜者灼龜佔之，公謹自外來見，遽投於地而進曰：「凡卜筮者，將以決嫌疑，定猶豫，今既事在不疑，何卜之有？
units.en: As the prince prepared to strike, a diviner was burning turtle shells; Gongjin threw them down and said: "Divination resolves doubt—there is no doubt here; why divine?
units.literal: When Taizong was about to punish Jiancheng and Yuanji, he sent a diviner to burn turtle and divine; Gongjin coming from outside saw this, hastily cast it to the ground and advanced: "All divination is to decide doubt and settle hesitation; now the affair is beyond doubt—why divine?

units.zh: 縱卜之不吉，勢不可已。
units.en: Even if the omen were bad, you cannot stop now.
units.literal: Even if divination were inauspicious, the momentum cannot be stopped.

units.zh: 願大王思之。」
units.en: Think on it, my lord."
units.literal: I wish the Great King to think on this."

units.zh: 太宗深然其言。
units.en: The prince was deeply convinced.
units.literal: Taizong deeply approved his words.

units.zh: 六月四日，公謹與長孫無忌等九人伏於玄武門以俟變。
units.en: On the fourth day of the sixth month Gongjin with Zhangsun Wuji, among a party of nine, lay in ambush at Xuanwu Gate awaiting the change.
units.literal: On the fourth day of the sixth month Gongjin with Zhangsun Wuji, among a party of nine, lay in ambush at Xuanwu Gate awaiting the change.

units.zh: 及斬建成、元吉，其黨來攻玄武門，兵鋒甚盛。
units.en: When the princes were killed, their followers assaulted Xuanwu Gate fiercely.
units.literal: When Jiancheng and Yuanji were beheaded, their faction came to attack Xuanwu Gate; the blades of war were very fierce.

units.zh: 公謹有勇力，獨閉門以拒之。
units.en: Gongjin alone barred the gate and held them off.
units.literal: Gongjin had courage and strength; alone he closed the gate to resist them.

units.zh: 以功累授左武候將軍，封定遠郡公，賜實封一千戶。
units.en: He was made left martial guard general, Duke of Dingyuan, with a thousand-household fief.
units.literal: For achievements he was repeatedly appointed Left Martial Guard General, enfeoffed as Duke of Dingyuan commandery, granted a substantive fief of a thousand households.

units.zh: 貞觀元年，拜代州都督，上表請置屯田以省轉運，又前後言時政得失十餘事，並見納用。
units.en: In Zhenguan 1 he governed Daizhou, proposed garrison farming to cut transport costs, and offered more than ten policy critiques—all adopted.
units.literal: In the first year of Zhenguan he was appointed Military Governor of Daizhou; he memorialized asking to establish garrison farming to save transport costs, and also spoke more than ten times on gains and losses of current policy before and after—all were accepted and used.

units.zh: 後遣李靖經略突厥，以公謹為副，公謹因言突厥可取之狀曰：「頡利縱慾肆情，窮凶極暴，誅害良善，暱近小人，此主昏於上，其可取一也。
units.en: As Li Jing's deputy against the Turks, he argued they could be taken, saying: "Jieli is tyrannical and muddled at the top—that is reason one.
units.literal: Later Li Jing strategized against the Turks; Gongjin was his deputy; Gongjin therefore stated the condition in which Turks could be taken: "Jieli indulges desires and acts wantonly, to the utmost cruel and violent, executing and harming the good, favoring petty men close at hand—this lord is muddled above; he can be taken for reason one.

units.zh: 又其別部同羅、僕骨、回紇、延陀之類，並自立君長，將圖反噬，此則眾叛於下，其可取二也。
units.en: Their tribes Tongluo, Pugu, Huihe, and Yantuo were setting up rival chiefs ready to rebel—reason two.
units.literal: Moreover his separate tribes Tongluo, Pugu, Huihe, Yantuo, and the like each set up their own lords and chiefs, about to turn and bite back—this is the masses rebelling below; he can be taken for reason two.

units.zh: 突厥被疑，輕騎自免；
units.en: Turk leaders fled in suspicion on light horses;
units.literal: The Turks are suspected; light cavalry escape on their own;

units.zh: 拓設出討，匹馬不歸；
units.en: the Tuo she campaign lost every horse;
units.literal: the Tuo she went out on campaign and not one horse returned;

units.zh: 欲谷喪師，立足無地，此則兵挫將敗，其可取三也。
units.en: Yugu lost his army and had nowhere to stand—reason three.
units.literal: Yugu lost his army and had no ground to stand on—this is troops defeated and generals broken; he can be taken for reason three.

units.zh: 塞北霜早，糧餱乏絕，其可取四也。
units.en: Early frost and famine in the north—reason four.
units.literal: North of the passes frost came early and grain rations were cut off; he can be taken for reason four.

units.zh: 頡利疏其突厥，親委諸胡，胡人翻覆，是其常性，大軍一臨，內必生變，其可取五也。
units.en: Jieli favored the Hu, who are treacherous by nature and would turn when the Tang army came—reason five.
units.literal: Jieli estranged his Turks and personally entrusted various Hu; the Hu are treacherous and that is their constant nature—when the great army arrives, within they will surely change; he can be taken for reason five.

units.zh: 華人入北，其類實多，比聞自相嘯聚，保據山險，師出塞垣，自然有應，其可取六也。」
units.en: Many Chinese in the north would rise when the army crossed the border—that is reason six."
units.literal: Chinese entering the north are very many in kind; recently heard they gather and roar among themselves, hold mountain passes and danger—when the army leaves the border wall, naturally there will be response; he can be taken for reason six.

units.zh: 太宗深納之。
units.en: The emperor accepted every point.
units.literal: Taizong deeply accepted this.

units.zh: 破定襄，敗頡利，璽書慰勞，進封鄒國公。
units.en: After Dingxiang and Jieli fell, he was advanced to Duke of Zou.
units.literal: Breaking Dingxiang and defeating Jieli, imperial writing comforted and rewarded him; he was advanced to Duke of Zou.

units.zh: 轉襄州都督，甚有惠政。
units.en: As military governor of Xiangzhou he ruled with notable kindness.
units.literal: Transferred to Military Governor of Xiangzhou, he had very benevolent government.

units.zh: 卒官，年三十九。
units.en: He died in office at thirty-nine.
units.literal: He died in office, aged thirty-nine.

units.zh: 太宗聞而嗟悼，出次發哀，有司奏言：「准《陰陽書》，日子在辰，不可哭泣，又為流俗所忌。」
units.en: The emperor mourned him; officials memorialized: "According to the Book of Yin and Yang, when the day stands in chen one must not weep—it is also tabooed by common custom."
units.literal: Taizong heard and sighed in grief; he went out to halt and hold mourning; the relevant office memorialized: "According to the Book of Yin and Yang, on days when the date is in chen one cannot weep; it is also tabooed by floating custom."

units.zh: 太宗曰：「君臣之義，同於父子，情發於衷，安避辰日？」
units.en: He replied: "Between ruler and minister and father and son, grief comes from the heart—why obey the almanac?"
