units.literal: Taizong said: "The righteousness of ruler and minister is the same as father and son; feeling issues from the breast—how avoid the day of chen?"

units.zh: 遂哭之。
units.en: And he wept.
units.literal: He then wept.

units.zh: 贈左驍衛大將軍，謚曰襄。
units.en: He was posthumously made left xiaoqi grand general with the name Xiang.
units.literal: Posthumously granted Left Xiaoqi Grand General, posthumous name Xiang.

units.zh: 十三年，追思舊功，改封郯國公。
units.en: In year 13 his title was changed to Duke of Tan in remembrance of his service.
units.literal: In the thirteenth year, recalling old achievements, his fief was changed to Duke of Tan.

units.zh: 十七年，圖形於凌煙閣。
units.en: In year 17 his portrait was painted at Lingyan Pavilion.
units.literal: In the seventeenth year his portrait was at Lingyan Pavilion.

units.zh: 永徽中，又贈荊州都督。
units.en: Under Yonghui he was posthumously made military governor of Jingzhou.
units.literal: In the Yonghui reign he was again posthumously granted Military Governor of Jingzhou.

units.zh: 長子大象嗣，官至戶部侍郎。
units.en: His eldest son Daxiang inherited and rose to vice minister of revenue.
units.literal: The eldest son Daxiang inherited, reaching Vice Minister of Revenue.

units.zh: 次子大素、大安，並知名。
units.en: His second sons Dasu and Da'an were both famous.
units.literal: The second sons Dasu and Da'an were both well known.

units.zh: 大素，龍朔中歷位東台舍人，兼修國史，卒於懷州長史，撰《後魏書》一百卷、《隋書》三十捲。
units.en: Dasu in the Longshuo reign served as Eastern Terrace Attendant and concurrently compiled the national history; he died as Chief Administrator of Huaizhou, having written the Book of Later Wei in 100 juan and the Book of Sui in 30 juan.
units.literal: Dasu in the Longshuo reign held office as Eastern Terrace Attendant, also editing the national history; he died as Chief Administrator of Huaizhou, compiling the Book of Later Wei in one hundred juan and the Book of Sui in thirty scrolls.

units.zh: 大安，上元中歷太子庶子、同中書門下三品。
units.en: Da'an was crown prince household subordinate and co-director of the Secretariat under Shangyuan.
units.literal: Da'an in the Shangyuan reign held office as Crown Prince Household Subordinate and Tong Zhongshu Menxia Sanpin.

units.zh: 時章懷太子在春宮，令大安與太子洗馬劉訥言等注范曄《後漢書》。
units.en: For Prince Zhanghuai he annotated Fan Ye's Book of Later Han with Liu Nayan and others.
units.literal: At the time Prince Zhanghuai was in the Eastern Palace; he ordered Da'an with Crown Prince Study Companion Liu Nayan and others to annotate Fan Ye's Book of Later Han.

units.zh: 宮廢，左授普州刺史。
units.en: When the eastern palace fell he was demoted to prefect of Pu.
units.literal: When the palace was abolished, he was demoted left to Prefect of Pu.

units.zh: 光宅中，卒於橫州司馬。
units.en: He died as administrator of Hengzhou under Guangzhai.
units.literal: In the Guangzhai reign he died as Administrator of Hengzhou.

units.zh: 大安子涚，開元中為國子祭酒。
units.en: Da'an's son Shui was chancellor of the directorate of education under Kaiyuan.
units.literal: Da'an's son Shui, in the Kaiyuan reign, was Chancellor of the Directorate of Education.

units.zh: 史臣曰：敬德奪槊陷陣，鼓勇王師，卻賂報恩，竭忠霸主。
units.en: The historian writes: Jingde seized lances, broke enemy lines, refused bribes, and served his lord with utter loyalty.
units.literal: The historiographer says: Jingde seized lances and broke formations, rousing courage in the King's army, refusing bribes and repaying favor, exhausting loyalty to the hegemon lord.

units.zh: 然而奮拳負氣，非自全之道；
units.en: Yet his proud temper was no way to preserve himself;
units.literal: Yet striking with fists and relying on spirit was not the way of self-preservation;

units.zh: 文皇告誡之言，可為功臣藥石。
units.en: Taizong's warning to him should be medicine for every meritorious minister.
units.literal: Wen Huang's admonishing words can serve as medicine and stone for meritorious ministers.

units.zh: 叔寶善用馬槊，拔賊壘則以寡敵眾，可謂勇矣。
units.en: Shubao mastered the lance and with few men stormed enemy walls—that was true courage.
units.literal: Shubao was skilled in using the mounted lance; pulling rebel ramparts he with few opposed many—this can be called brave.

units.zh: 知節志平國難，拜隼籞則致命輔君，可謂忠矣。
units.en: Zhijie sought to end the realm's crisis and, once in imperial service, gave his life to his sovereign—truly loyal.
units.literal: Zhijie aspired to pacify the state's hardship; bowing at the falcon-perch office he gave his life to assist the lord—this can be called loyal.

units.zh: 而並曉世充之猜貳，識唐代之霸圖，可謂見幾君子矣。
units.en: Both saw through Wang Shichong's deceit and recognized the Tang's destiny—men who read the times aright.
units.literal: Moreover both understood Shichong's suspicion and division and recognized the Tang age's hegemonic design—this can be called gentlemen who see the first signs.

units.zh: 志玄中鏑不言，竟安師旅。
units.en: Zhixuan took an arrow in silence and thereby steadied the army.
units.literal: Zhixuan was struck by an arrowhead yet did not speak, and in the end secured the army brigades.

units.zh: 公謹投龜定議，志助儲君。
units.en: Gongjin cast aside divination to fix the coup and devoted himself to the heir apparent.
units.literal: Gongjin cast aside the turtle and settled the plan, his will set on assisting the heir.

units.zh: 皆所謂猛將謀臣，知機識變。
units.en: All were fierce generals and shrewd advisers who grasped the moment and adapted to change.
units.literal: All are what are called fierce generals and plotting ministers, knowing the moment and recognizing change.

units.zh: 有唐之盛，斯實賴焉。
units.en: The greatness of Tang owed much to men such as these.
units.literal: The Tang's flourishing truly relied on this.

units.zh: 贊曰：太宗經綸，實賴虎臣。
units.en: Eulogy: Taizong's founding of the empire rested on tiger-like champions.
units.literal: Eulogy says: Taizong's weaving of the realm truly relied on tiger ministers.

units.zh: 胡、鄂諸將，奮不顧身。
units.en: The dukes of Hu and E and their peers fought without thought for their lives.
units.literal: The generals of Hu and E and the rest strove without regard for their persons.

units.zh: 圖形凌煙，配食嚴禋。
units.en: Their faces were painted at Lingyan Pavilion; they shared in the grand state sacrifices.
units.literal: Their portraits were painted at Lingyan; they received sacrificial shares in the solemn suburban sacrifices.

units.zh: 光諸簡冊，為報君親。
units.en: Their glory shines in the histories as repayment to sovereign and father.
units.literal: They glorify the various bamboo slips and registers, repaying ruler and kin.
